chapters.title: Brands and portals
intro: This chapter is for administrators. It explains how to set up a brand and its customer help center, also called the portal.
It also covers logos, footers, the default brand and using your own domain name for the help center.

sections.title: How brands work
intro: A brand is a name your customers know you by. Each brand has its own help center, colours, logo, e-mail footer and sender name.
Channels, knowledge base categories and tickets belong to a brand. Customers see only the help center of their brand.
blocks: To open the list, select **Administration** > **Brands & portals**. You need the **Manage departments, teams, brands and calendars** permission.

blocks.caption: The **Brands & portals** page with one brand.
blocks.alt: Brands and portals page with numbered highlights on New brand, the brand banner, the brand title with its badges, the portal address and the Edit and menu buttons

callouts: The banner in the brand's colours, with its logo or first letter.
The brand name. **Default** marks the main brand. **Portal on** or **Portal off** shows whether the help center is online.
The portal address. Select it to open the help center in a new tab.
**Edit** opens the brand. The menu button has more actions.

blocks.heading: How many brands you can have

blocks: A second brand needs the multi-brand feature of your plan. The Trial plan allows 2 brands, Starter 1, Professional 3 and Enterprise any number.

sections.title: The brand page
sections.intro: Select **Edit** on a brand to open its page. The page has five cards and a live preview of the help center.

blocks.caption: The brand page of the default brand.
blocks.alt: Brand page with numbered highlights on the Identity, Logo and favicon, Custom domain, Portal and Contact and footers cards, the preview and the save bar

callouts: **Logo & favicon**: the images of the brand.
**Custom domain**: your own address for the help center.
**Portal**: the help center's title, languages, sign-in and features.
**Contact & footers**: support contacts and the footers of the portal and e-mails.
The preview shows the colours, title and welcome message as you type.
The save bar with **Discard** and **Save brand**.

blocks: The save bar shows **Unsaved changes** until you save. **Open portal** at the top right opens the help center.

sections.title: Create a brand
sections.intro: Create a brand for a new company name or product line with its own help center.
prerequisites: You have the **Manage departments, teams, brands and calendars** permission.
steps: Select **Administration** > **Brands & portals**, then select **New brand**.

steps.text: Enter the **Brand name**. SupportDesk fills in the **Portal address** from the name.
steps.caption: The **Identity** card of a new brand.
steps.alt: Identity card with Brand name Wings Retail, Portal address wings-retail, Primary colour and Accent colour

steps: Change the **Portal address** if you want a different one. The hint shows the full address.
Choose the **Primary colour** and the **Accent colour**. Use the colour picker or type a code such as `#2563eb`.
In the **Portal** card, enter the **Portal title** and the **Default language**.
Fill in the other cards as needed. See the sections below.
Select **Create brand**.
sections.result: The app shows **Brand created**. You can now upload the logo and favicon.

sections.title: Identity fields
sections.intro: These fields are in the **Identity** card.

rows: The short name in the help center address. Use 2 to 64 lower-case letters, digits and hyphens. It must be unique across SupportDesk.
The main colour of the help center, such as the header. Use a colour code such as `#2563eb`.
The colour of buttons and links. Use a colour code such as `#0ea5e9`.

blocks.note: Some words are reserved and cannot be portal addresses, such as `admin`, `portal` and `widget`.

sections.title: Add a logo and favicon
sections.intro: The logo appears in the help center header and in e-mails. The favicon is the small icon in the browser tab.
prerequisites: The brand is saved. New brands show the upload buttons after you create them.
You have a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP image of 2 MB or less.
steps: Open the brand.
In the **Logo & favicon** card, select **Upload** next to **Logo**.
Choose the image file. A wide image works best for the logo.
Select **Upload** next to **Favicon** and choose a square image, such as 64 × 64 pixels.
sections.result: The app shows **Logo uploaded** or **Favicon uploaded**. The images appear in the card and in the preview.
blocks: To remove an image, select **Remove** next to it.

blocks.note: SupportDesk checks every uploaded image for malware before it uses it.

sections.title: Set up the help center
sections.intro: The **Portal** card decides what customers see and can do in the brand's help center.
steps: Open the brand and find the **Portal** card.
Enter the **Portal title** and an optional **Welcome message**.
In **Default department for portal tickets**, choose a department. Or keep **Routing decides**.
Enter the **Default language**, such as `en`, and add other codes in **Languages offered**.
Choose how customers sign in, in **Customer sign-in**.
Turn on **Help center is online**.
Turn on the features you want customers to use.
Select **Save brand**.
sections.result: The app shows **Brand saved**. Changes, including the colours, apply in the help center at once.

blocks.caption: The **Portal** card with the help center online.
blocks.alt: Portal card with Portal title, Default department for portal tickets, Welcome message, Default language, Languages offered, Customer sign-in and the feature switches

blocks.note: The feature switches are greyed out while **Help center is online** is off. The default brand's help center cannot be switched off.

sections.title: Help center options
sections.intro: These switches and lists are in the **Portal** card.

rows: Lets customers ask and answer questions.
Lets customers chat with agents from the help center.
Answers from the knowledge base before a customer raises a ticket.
Lets visitors raise tickets without signing in. It needs the help center to be online.
Lets customers create their own help center account.
**E-mail and password / one-time code**, **Single sign-on only** or **Both**.
Where tickets from the help center go. **Routing decides** uses your routing rules.
Up to 20 language codes, such as `en`, `fr` or `pt-BR`.

blocks.note: Customer single sign-on is not available yet. With **Single sign-on only**, the help center hides the password option, and customers sign in with e-mail codes.

sections.title: Set contact details and footers
sections.intro: Add your support contacts and the footers that appear in the help center and in e-mails for this brand.
steps: Open the brand and find the **Contact & footers** card.
Enter the **Support e-mail** and the **Support phone**.

steps.note: The help center keeps links, formatting and images in the footer. It removes any other code.

steps: Enter the **E-mail footer / signature (HTML)**.
Check the **E-mail footer preview** below the fields.
Select **Save brand**.
sections.result: The e-mail footer is added to replies, acknowledgements and surveys sent for this brand.

blocks.caption: The **Contact & footers** card with the e-mail footer preview.
blocks.alt: Contact and footers card with Support e-mail, Support phone, Portal footer, E-mail footer and its preview

blocks.tip: Ask someone who knows HTML to write the footers. Plain text also works.

sections.title: Use your own domain for the help center
sections.intro: A custom domain shows the help center under your own address, such as `support.example.com`.
prerequisites: Someone in your company can change your domain's DNS settings, the address book of your web addresses.
steps: Open the brand and find the **Custom domain** card.

steps.text: In **Domain**, enter the address without `https://`, such as `support.example.com`.
steps.caption: The **Custom domain** card with a domain typed in but not yet saved.
steps.alt: Custom domain card with the Domain field filled in

steps: Select **Save brand**. The card now shows the **DNS record to create**.
Give the **Type**, **Name** and **Points to** values to your IT team. They create the record.
After they finish, select **Check DNS**.
sections.result: The badge shows **Connected** when the domain points to SupportDesk. **Points elsewhere** or **Not found** means the record is wrong or not active yet.

blocks.warning: In this release, the help center does not yet open on custom domains. Keep sharing the standard portal address. E-mail links for a brand with a custom domain use that domain, so they do not work yet.

blocks.note: **Check DNS** only compares addresses. It does not prove that you own the domain. Your IT team must also set up a security certificate for the domain.

sections.title: Open a help center or change the default brand
sections.intro: The default brand is your main brand. New channels use it unless you choose another brand.
steps: Select **Administration** > **Brands & portals**.

steps.text: Select the menu button on the brand's card.
steps.caption: The brand menu.
steps.alt: Menu with Open the portal, Make default brand and Delete

steps: Choose **Open the portal** to see the help center in a new tab.
Choose **Make default brand** to make this brand the main brand.
sections.result: The app shows **Default brand changed**. The **Default** badge moves to this brand.

blocks.note: **Make default brand** is greyed out while the brand's help center is offline. Turn on **Help center is online** first.

sections.title: Take a help center offline or delete a brand
sections.intro: Switch a help center off when you stop using a brand. Delete a brand only if it has no tickets and no channels.
steps: To take the help center offline, open the brand, turn off **Help center is online** and select **Save brand**.
To delete a brand, select **Delete** in its menu on the **Brands & portals** page.
In the confirmation, type the brand's portal address to confirm.
Select **Delete**.
sections.result: The app shows **Brand deleted**, and its help center stops working.

blocks.warning: You cannot undo a delete. You cannot delete the default brand, a brand with tickets or a brand with channels. Move its channels to another brand, or switch its help center off instead.

troubleshooting.problem: The app says the portal address is already taken.
troubleshooting.cause: Another workspace or brand uses that address.
troubleshooting.fix: Choose another **Portal address**, for example by adding your city or product.

troubleshooting.problem: The app says the address is reserved.
troubleshooting.cause: SupportDesk uses that word itself, such as `admin` or `portal`.
Your plan allows a set number of brands.
troubleshooting.fix: Delete or reuse a brand you do not need, or ask for a bigger plan.

troubleshooting.problem: **Help center is online** cannot be switched off.
troubleshooting.cause: It is the default brand. Its help center must stay online.
troubleshooting.fix: Make another brand the default first.

troubleshooting.cause: The brand's help center is offline.
troubleshooting.fix: Turn on **Help center is online**, save, and try again.

troubleshooting.cause: It is the default brand, or tickets or channels belong to it.
troubleshooting.fix: Move its channels to another brand, or switch its help center off instead.

troubleshooting.cause: The file is over 2 MB, or it is not a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP image.
troubleshooting.fix: Make the image smaller or save it in a supported format.

troubleshooting.problem: The app says the domain is already used.
troubleshooting.cause: Another help center uses that domain.
troubleshooting.fix: Use a different domain, or remove it from the other brand first.

troubleshooting.cause: The DNS record points to another address, or the change has not spread yet.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask your IT team to check the record against the **Points to** value. Wait an hour and check again.

faq.q: Can customers use our own domain for the help center now?
faq.a: Not yet. You can save the domain and check its DNS record, but customers must use the standard portal address for now.

faq.q: Do brands share the knowledge base?
faq.a: Yes, unless you limit a category to some brands. A category's **Brands** setting decides which help centers show it.

faq.q: What happens to tickets of a brand whose help center is offline?
faq.a: Nothing. Agents keep working on them. Customers of that brand can no longer use the help center.

glossary.definition: A company or product name with its own help center, colours, logo and e-mail identity.
The customer portal of a brand, where customers read articles, raise tickets and follow them.
The short name in a help center's web address, such as `wings`.
The main brand of the workspace. Its help center must stay online.
Your own web address for a help center, such as `support.example.com`.
An entry in your domain's settings that tells browsers where an address points.
The small icon that browsers show in the tab of a web page.
